skills.name: A formal letter about a school concern

note.text: A formal letter addresses a person in an official role. State the purpose clearly, describe a specific concern and request a realistic response. Use a respectful tone and organised paragraphs. Distinguish observed facts from reports or opinions. Avoid naming classmates in unsupported accusations. School conventions for addresses, date, subject and closing should be confirmed by the teacher. This task uses an imaginary school and writer.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Original model: Dear Principal, I am writing about damage to materials in the shared reading room. During recent meetings, books have been left near an uncovered window. I request a dry storage shelf and a reminder about returning materials safely. These steps could help everyone use the books. Thank you for considering the request. Yours faithfully, Bih.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify the recipient, concern, evidence and proposed remedy. Remove insults and guesses presented as facts. Check the salutation and closing against the convention taught in class. A respectful request is stronger when its practical purpose is easy to identify.

paper_task.prompt: Write a formal letter from an imaginary learner to a school authority about a behaviour affecting shared school resources. Describe the concern without unsupported allegations and propose a remedy.
model: Dear Principal, I am writing about damage to materials in the shared reading room. During recent meetings, books have been left near an uncovered window. I request a dry storage shelf and a reminder about returning materials safely. These steps could help everyone use the books. Thank you for considering the request. Yours faithfully, Bih.
checklist: My purpose and recipient are clear.
I distinguish observations from opinions or rumours.
My request is practical and politely expressed.
I have checked the teacher's formal-letter conventions.
